Definition: emptiness; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain
BiblicalUsage: The word rîyq means emptiness; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain. In Habakkuk 2:13, we read, "…very fire, and the people shall weary themselves…"; in Isaiah 30:7, "…cried concerning this, Their strength to sit still". You hear it again in Jeremiah 51:34 — "Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me…" — and in Job 39:16, "…is hardened against her young ones, as though…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rîyq matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. And I believe rîyq still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
